newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile blue chips end firm, Unimarc boosts volume.
newsitem.headline: Chile blue chips end firm, Unimarc boosts volume.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed stronger, hitting their highest point this year, in otherwise light trade boosted by heavy dealing in Wall Street debutante supermarket chain Unimarc, said traders.
The 40-share index ended unofficially up 0.44 percent at 120.6 points.
The general index rose 0.36 percent to 5,388.98 points.
Turnover swelled to 14 billion pesos from nine billion pesos Thursday, but was bolstered by a six billion peso local stock offering from supermarket chain Unimarc.

Unimarc's American Depositary Receipts and stocks rose sharply on strong demand from foreign investors who have made profits from other supermarket stocks, including Santa Isabel and D&S, said Henry Rudnick of CB Capitales.
"People who have done well in the sector hope to repeat the success of companies like Santa Isabel," he said.
Unimarc closed at 153.5 pesos after opening at a minimum price of 140 pesos.
The bolsa is expected to resume its upward tilt at Monday's opening, although the light volume means the rally has little real support and the bolsa could soon suffer a correction, said dealers.
Losers included copper products maker Madeco, down 2.97 percent at 1,145 pesos and Banco Sud Americano A series shares which shed 2.25 percent to 130 pesos.
